newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian shares power upwards in bumper turnover.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian shares power upwards in bumper turnover.

text.p: Norwegian shares scaled to new highs on Tuesday buoyed by good liquidity, a firm dollar and healthy sentiment on foreign markets, dealers said.
Mergers in Sweden's banking sector and speculation of consolidation in Norway's finance industry added to the upward momentum, they said. Oslo's banking index added 3.42 percent to 116.89 percent.
"We are carrying on the positive trend from before but there are also a lot of fresh positive signals adding to that trend," said one broker, who expected the market to continue to gain ground.
Oslo's Total share index advanced 1.09 percent to close at a new record 1,114.22 points after hitting an intraday peak at 1,114.93 points. Turnover was a bumper 1.53 billion crowns.

Power producer Hafslund was the most heavily traded stock in a total of 250 million crowns turnover after state oil company Statoil exchanged 2.69 million B shares for an equivalent number of A shares.
Statoil now has 16.7 percent of Hafslund voting shares. A Statoil spokesman said it intended to focus on energy.
On Wednesday Saga, Christiania Bank, Nycomed and Dyno will release results.
